primary_citation: 18 U.S.C. §§3121-3127 (Pen Register Act, Title III of ECPA, Pub. L. 99-508 (1986); amended by USA PATRIOT Act, Pub. L. 107-56 (2001))
short_title: Pen Register Act / ECPA Title III — Routing Metadata Protection; Evidence Framework (No Civil Damages)
one_line_rule: Installing or using a pen register or trap and trace device without a court order or user consent is prohibited; the Pen Register Act covers routing metadata (who called whom, IP addresses, email headers) but NOT communication content; no private civil damages — criminal enforcement only; critical as an evidence framework for quantifying SIM swap violations under §2511 and CIPA.

case_law.court: Supreme Court of the United States
case_law.key_rule: No Fourth Amendment protection for telephone numbers dialed (pen register metadata); third-party doctrine applies; prompted Congress to create ECPA Title III (1986) statutory protection. Limited by Carpenter v. United States (2018) for comprehensive CSLI — Smith not overruled but narrowed.

case_law.cite: United States v. Forrester, 512 F.3d 500 (9th Cir. 2008) (URL question); In re Application for Pen Register, 396 F. Supp. 2d 747 (S.D. Tex. 2005)
case_law.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit; United States District Court, S.D. Texas
case_law.key_rule: IP addresses and email headers = routing information (Pen Register Act); URL paths potentially content (Wiretap Act) — 9th Circuit left URL question unresolved. Critical for classification of SIM swap account access records and damages theory.

evidence_framework_application.no_civil_damages: §3121 has NO civil damages provision — all civil remedies flow from §2511 (Wiretap), §2701 (SCA), and CIPA §632.7
evidence_framework_application.critical_evidence_value: Call routing records documenting SIM swap period = essential evidence for per-violation damages calculation under §2511 ($10K/event) and CIPA ($5K/event)
evidence_framework_application.civil_subpoena_path: AT&T call records obtainable through civil discovery subpoena (not just government §2703 process); routing logs show which calls were diverted during SIM swap
evidence_framework_application.url_content_argument: If SSA disability portal and financial account URL accesses during hijacked session = content under Wiretap Act → additional §2511 violations at $10,000/event beyond the base SIM swap interception theory
evidence_framework_application.criminal_referral: §3121 criminal violation by SIM swap = law enforcement referral pathway; government prosecution of McClaran for pen register violation + §2511 would provide additional civil leverage
evidence_framework_application.carpenter_extension: Carpenter v. United States (2018) logic potentially applies to comprehensive SIM swap routing surveillance — ongoing monitoring through redirected SIM may require higher legal protection analysis
